name: Marrakech
title: Holidays in Marrakech
intro: Snake charmers, rooftop pools and the Atlas Mountains on the horizon, a short flight from the UK. Here's what Marrakech is like with the family and when to go.

facts.label: Time difference
facts.value: 0 to 1 hr ahead of the UK

facts_note: Dirhams can only be bought in Morocco. Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: Spring and autumn are best, with warm sunny days and comfortable evenings. July and August are very hot, so pick a riad with a pool. Winter days are sunny but nights are cold, and there may be snow on the mountains. Ramadan moves each year and changes opening hours.

things.name: Jemaa el-Fnaa
things.blurb: The main square fills with storytellers, acrobats and food stalls as the sun sets.

things.name: Jardin Majorelle
things.blurb: A blue and yellow garden full of cactuses. Book a timed ticket.

things.name: The souks
things.blurb: A maze of stalls selling lamps, slippers and spices. Agree a price before you buy.

things.name: Agafay Desert
things.blurb: A stony desert about 40 minutes away for camel rides and quad bikes.

things.name: Atlas Mountains
things.blurb: Walk to waterfalls in the Ourika Valley or Imlil, with lunch in a Berber village.

things.name: Le Jardin Secret
things.blurb: A peaceful garden in the medina with a tower to climb.

faqs.question: Is Marrakech good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes, for families who like something different. It's colourful and exciting, but the medina is busy and noisy, so a riad or hotel with a pool gives everyone a break.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: Four or five nights covers the city and a day in the mountains or desert. Some families add a few days on the coast at Essaouira.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: No, British passport holders can visit for up to 90 days without a visa. Passports must be valid for your whole stay. Check GOV.UK for the current rules.

faqs.question: What should we wear?
faqs.answer: Loose clothes that cover shoulders and knees are best in the medina and are cooler in the heat. Swimwear is fine at hotel pools.
